applyTo: "src/Presentation*/**/*.cs,src/Clients/Client/**/*.cs,src/Clients/Client.Desktop/**/*.cs"

# MVVM conventions

Presentation code uses **CommunityToolkit.Mvvm** with the
`Automaticks.CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Analyzers` rule pack. ViewModels are the
**only** layer that adapts domain state into bindable surfaces; Views bind, they
do not reach.

## ViewModel construction

- Inherit `ObservableObject` (or a sealed base) and use
  `[ObservableProperty]` for bindable state and `[RelayCommand]` for commands.
  Source generators handle the `INotifyPropertyChanged` plumbing — never write
  the backing field plus setter pair by hand.
- Backing fields generated by `[ObservableProperty]` are `_camelCase`.
- ViewModels are **Transient** — one per View instance. They implement
  `IDisposable` and the View detaches them on unload.
- The DI container resolves ViewModels through the locator in
  `Presentation`; never instantiate a ViewModel with `new` inside a code-behind.

## ViewModel ↔ domain boundary

ViewModels project **immutable** data classes out of the domain — they do not
hold a reference to a mutable domain object. The typical shape:

- Domain model: `TrafficFlow`, `WebSocketFlow`, `RemoteProcedureCallFlow`,
  `BreakpointPause`, … (mutable, lives in `Domain.*`).
- Bindable projection: a `record` carrying the read-only data the View needs.
- The ViewModel subscribes to `IDomainEventBus` (or the appropriate
  `*Changed` event), rebuilds the projection, and assigns it through the
  generated setter so the binding refreshes.

A ViewModel may store primitives, enums, value tuples, and other ViewModels,
but it **must not** hold a direct reference to a `Domain.<Context>` mutable
type. This keeps the View thread-safe against background mutation of the
underlying flow, and avoids accidental edits-through-binding.

## Command rules

- `[RelayCommand]` methods take at most one argument and return `Task`,
  `Task<T>`, or `void`. Long-running async commands accept a
  `CancellationToken`.
- Use method-group references in XAML (`Command="{Binding SaveCommand}"`),
  never inline lambdas at construction.
- Commands surface user-facing errors through the dialog/overlay/messaging
  infrastructure in `Presentation`. Never `throw` from a command — translate to
  a notification.

## Cross-VM communication

ViewModels never reference each other directly. Cross-VM coordination uses
`CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Messaging.WeakReferenceMessenger`:

- The publisher sends a strongly-typed message
  (`MessengerInstance.Send(new TrafficFlowSelected(flow.Id))`).
- The subscriber registers in its constructor and unregisters in `Dispose`.
- Messages are records, named after the **event** (past tense), not the action.

Domain events (raised through `IDomainEventBus`) are an option when the trigger
originates in a domain change, not a UI gesture; otherwise prefer `IMessenger`.

## UI-thread marshaling

- All mutations of `[ObservableProperty]`-generated state happen on the UI
  thread.
- After `await` of a non-UI task, hop back through `Dispatcher.UIThread.Post`
  / `InvokeAsync` before assigning a bound property.
- `ObservableCollection<T>` mutations must occur on the UI thread; either
  marshal each `Add` / `Remove`, or use a buffered queue flushed from a UI-thread
  callback. The `Framework` project ships observable-collection helpers used
  by `Presentation.Traffic` — prefer them over rolling your own.

## Suspending notifications

When loading or replacing a large collection, suspend notifications around the
mutation to avoid an `INotifyPropertyChanged` storm. Pair every suspend with a
resume in `try`/`finally` so an exception in the middle of a load cannot leak.

## Validation

ValidationViewModels rely on `INotifyDataErrorInfo` (provided by
`ObservableValidator` from the toolkit). Validation rules live in the
ViewModel — the View shows the error, the domain refuses the operation. Never
re-implement a domain invariant in the ViewModel; project the failure from a
`Result<T>` instead.

## Dialogs, overlays, notifications

- Modal dialogs are last-resort; prefer non-modal overlays and toast-style
  notifications.
- Dialogs are presented through the shared `Presentation` dialog handler.
  ViewModels request a dialog via the handler interface, then react to the
  returned `Result<DialogOutcome>`.
- Never call `MessageBox` / `IDialogService` directly from a code-behind.

## Localisation

Bound user-visible strings go through the `Resources/` ResourceManager — see
`localization.instructions.md`. Keys follow `{Feature}_{Context}_{Element}`.
ViewModels expose a localised string by referencing the resource key, not by
hard-coding English. The text properties on a ViewModel that are computed
(`{Count} flows captured`) format from the resource template and the live data.

## Threading and disposal

- ViewModels that subscribe to long-lived sources (`IDomainEventBus`,
  `IMessenger`, file watchers) must dispose the subscription in `Dispose`.
- Background loops started from a ViewModel are cancelled through a
  `CancellationTokenSource` owned by the ViewModel and cancelled in `Dispose`.
- Never call `Task.Run` from a ViewModel to "make it async" — call the async
  method and `await` it.
